chapter: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
title: His current small-group scoring and organ voicings
summary: He is writing for about eight pieces like the Kansas City Six, and plays tenor trombone, drums, piano and organ in a tightly arranged quartet.

bands.name: Bon Bon Tunnell and His Buddies

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I will, because that -- see, I'm writing a score now for about eight pieces. Like I did with the Kansas City Six and the -- Bob Barney's Buddies, but for what I got in mind I need another couple of more instruments, maybe one more, because I got a particular sound I want to get and I had my guitar special built for it, but I don't use it in public.
What instrumentation have you got for this eight pieces?

Out there, using a tenor trombone and drums, piano, which is using an organ sometimes, piano and then a little organ. Four of us, most times. When five come in, it sounds like a full band, but even a four fills up because everything's organized. We got introductions and endings and all to it. Nobody looks at nobody. Everything's all chopped up, everything we do -- Mood Indigo and the ______, we just get a standing ovation on that.
Yeah, because, you see, I know how to
voice the organ with the clarinet and the trombone. We play it, it sounds -- it's beautiful.
Well, that's good. It should be very nice.
